puppeteer_navigate.rationale: `Navigate to a URL` with `URL to navigate to` lets the agent cause a browser request to an agent-chosen URL/host. That request is an attacker-readable destination when the URL is attacker-controlled, so it is a SINK. It also changes browser state, so kind is WRITE. `launchOptions` can restart the browser but the advertised text does not say this returns page content or executes arbitrary host code.

puppeteer_screenshot.rationale: `Take a screenshot of the current page or a specific element` and `capture the screenshot as a base64-encoded data URI (as text) instead of binary image content` indicate the tool returns captured page content. If the current page is an attacker-controlled web page, that returned content is UNTRUSTED. If the browser can view `file://`, localhost, intranet, or authenticated pages, the screenshot can return non-public content, so SECRET is kept; the advertised text does not state URL-scheme, network, or credential isolation limits, so this is undetermined. `Name for the screenshot` indicates creation of a named screenshot artifact, so kind is WRITE.

puppeteer_click.rationale: `Click an element on the page` sends a browser UI action to the current page. Because the current page may be an attacker-controlled page reached by URL navigation, the click can trigger form submission, navigation, or script-controlled requests to an attacker-readable destination. The `selector` decides which page element/action is invoked. No advertised result content is described.

puppeteer_fill.rationale: `Fill out an input field` with `Value to fill` sends agent-supplied text into the current page. If that page is attacker-controlled, page JavaScript or later form submission can read the value, making it a SINK. The `selector` chooses the destination field and `value` is the content sent.

puppeteer_select.rationale: `Select an element on the page with Select tag` with `Value to select` sends an agent-supplied selection value into the current page. If that page is attacker-controlled, page JavaScript or later submission can read it, so this is a SINK. The `selector` chooses the destination element and `value` is the content sent.

puppeteer_hover.rationale: `Hover an element on the page` sends a browser UI event to the current page. On an attacker-controlled page, hover handlers can observe the action and trigger requests or other writes to attacker-readable destinations, potentially using data already placed in the page. The `selector` chooses the element/action invoked. No advertised result content is described.

puppeteer_evaluate.rationale: `Execute JavaScript in the browser console` with `JavaScript code to execute` can run agent-supplied browser-page code. Such code can read and return page-controlled DOM/text, making outputs UNTRUSTED on attacker-controlled pages. If the current page is `file://`, localhost, intranet, or authenticated content, the same browser-console code can return non-public data, so SECRET is kept; the advertised text does not state page/network/credential isolation or exact return semantics, so this is undetermined. The script can also initiate browser requests or modify pages, and the `script` itself can contain both destination and content, so it is a SINK. This is not HOSTEXEC because the advertised execution is in the `browser console`, not arbitrary host execution.

value_conditions.effect: Dangerous Puppeteer launch options such as `--no-sandbox` are rejected; this limits reduced browser sandboxing but does not remove the SINK label for navigation.
